notes:
• A PR that still needs a review can be merged from Stellwerk when you may bypass the branch's rules (a ruleset's bypass list): the git bar says "PR review required, you can bypass it" and offers Merge on every app.
• A tap on an image in a chat opens the viewer on all of the chat's images (prompts' attachments and the agent's images, not those of tool calls), not just its message's. On the Mac the viewer shows them all as a strip at the bottom to click through, next to the arrows and the ← → keys; iPhone and Android swipe through them.
• Settings → Agents → "Permission mode" → Auto runs agents with their own safety checks instead of skipping permissions. Claude runs in Claude Code's auto mode, and when its classifier blocks something the chat waits for you to allow or deny it (iOS, Android, Mac). Codex runs in its sandbox (the workspace, the repository's .git and the project's extra folders), and its auto reviewer decides approvals, shown as rows in the chat.
• Dashboards get the Mac window's color theme: every page has `--stellwerk-*` CSS variables (22 colors and the font, light and dark under `prefers-color-scheme`, which follows Stellwerk's Light / Dark / System), `data-stellwerk-theme` / `data-stellwerk-scheme` on `<html>`, `window.stellwerk.theme` and a `stellwerk:theme` event when the theme changes, live without a reload. Mac only, like the dashboards.
• Links like Conductor's: `stellwerk://chat/<chat id>` opens a chat on whichever paired Mac has it, switching to that Mac (a closed one comes back as a tab), `stellwerk://new?repo=…&prompt=…&branch=…` opens New workspace with the message box filled in, without sending. Every chat's menu has **Copy chat link**, and agents learn both links from the Stellwerk skill. On the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android.
• Dashboards in the Mac window: Settings → Dashboards takes web pages with a title, URL and icon. Each one is a row in the sidebar above the projects, scrolling with them (in the order dragged into place there, ⌘⌥1–9), and shows the page in place of the chat, with back, forward, reload and "Open in browser"; the 3 most recent pages stay loaded for up to 10 minutes off screen. Links to other sites open in the browser. Mac only for now: the dashboards live in the Mac window's settings, so iPhone, iPad and Android don't show them.
• Mac: images in a chat can be saved. Right-click one for **Save to Downloads** (numbered like the Finder's copies when the name is taken, the Dock's Downloads stack bounces), **Save As…** and **Copy Image**, always the original file, not the thumbnail. The image viewer has a Save to Downloads button next to Share (⌘S); "Saved to Downloads" shows for a moment, a click on it shows the file in the Finder. iPhone, iPad and Android already save from their image viewer (Share → Save Image, Save Image).
• Pi as a third agent beside Claude Code and Codex, for local models: with Pi on the Mac, every model LM Studio or Ollama on it has shows in the model picker on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android without configuring anything (a bundled Pi extension asks them), e.g. "gemma-4-26b-a4b (LM Studio)", next to Pi's other models (`~/.pi/agent/models.json`, signed-in providers). An LM Studio model that isn't loaded gets loaded before Pi talks to it, with 64K tokens of context (`STELLWERK_LOCAL_CONTEXT`). Pi chats run `pi --mode rpc`, resume from Pi's session file, steer while working, stop, show thinking levels for models that think and answer extension dialogs as questions; branch names come from the chat's model. Enabling Entire in a project also adds Pi's extension; Pi 1.x chats trust the workspace's own `.pi` (`--approve`) so it loads. Not yet in Pi chats: plan mode, going back to a turn, usage limits. Pi chats can use the web through `stellwerk-browser`, a small CLI after Mario Zechner's browser-tools: a private headless Chrome per workspace with a fresh profile (none of your logins) beside your own Chrome, for searching (DuckDuckGo), reading pages, clicking, typing, JavaScript and screenshots, without MCP, API keys or Claude; Pi learns it from a few lines in its system prompt. Its Chrome ends with the chat or after 15 idle minutes, the profile with it. Without Chrome, search and read fall back to plain HTTP. Searches and page reads show like Claude's Web Search and Fetch.
• Projects get their own defaults (Settings → the project on the Mac): one of the Mac's presets (Default models; e.g. a local model through Pi) that new workspaces in the project start with on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android instead of the Mac's default; and, with more than one Claude account, the account the project's Claude chats run on, whichever one is active for the rest (switching it moves the project's chats like switching the active account).
• The agent's question works like Conductor's: one question at a time with dots to jump between them, picking the answer of a one-answer question moves on to the next (and from the last, with all answered, sends the answers), "Other…" moves on with return (pasted lines keep their line breaks), chosen options stand out with a check, and an X at the top right stops the agent like the stop button. On the Mac the card takes the keys when it comes, unless there's text in the message box or another field has them (then Tab in the message box hands them over): ↑ ↓ over the options, ↵ or space picks (toggles on multi-select), 1–9 and 0 for "Other…", ← → between questions, ⌘↵ sends, esc goes back to the message box, as does answering or stopping. iPhone and Android get the same card without the keys.
• Scripts can come from `.stellwerk/settings.toml`: Stellwerk reads it first and uses the committed `.conductor/settings.toml` only where a repository has none, so a repository can give Stellwerk its own setup, run and archive scripts while Conductor keeps reading `.conductor/`.
• Mac: Claude's file tools no longer write outside the workspace or to Claude Code's settings files (Claude Code 2.1.314+). Settings → Agents → "File edits only inside the workspace" turns this off, and a project's "Folders agents may edit" allows more folders. The Usage tab warns from ten days before Claude Code's login ends.
• Mac: when git can't run because the Xcode license isn't agreed to or the Command Line Tools are missing, the setup's Accounts step says so and fixes it, and failed imports and other git errors show git's own message instead of "LoginShell.Failure error 1".
• Mac: the experimental "Listen on all interfaces" switch is gone; the host is reachable only through Tailscale Serve, so the token never crosses the LAN in plain http. The Operator's tools use a token of their own that opens nothing else.
• Mac: a chat link to the workspace already open leaves a dashboard, Search or a draft on screen and shows the chat.
• Codex in auto mode can no longer change the repository's git config or hooks from its sandbox. Android build tools updated.
• Phones: over the saved copy the notice shows at once ("Connecting… · showing what was there at 10:42"), not only after several failed loads, and says "Offline" sooner (12 s per try instead of 45 s). Below it "Trying again in 8 s" and a Retry button. While the saved copy shows, a workspace's working ring stands still in grey and a chat's working mark turns into a dotted circle, since that agent may be done by now. iOS and Android.
• Mac, Settings → Operator: clearer text under "Pick up new to-dos". It now says the Operator handles small to-dos itself, starts a workspace for bigger ones or asks you first, and that with the switch off new to-dos just stay in the list.
• Mac: the PR button at the top right of the right panel sits as far from the window's right edge as from its top, so it fits evenly into the window's rounded corner, like in Conductor.
• Mac: a working workspace in the sidebar shows a ring turning around its glyph in the theme's accent color, like on the phone, instead of the small spinner.
• Mac: the PR button with a ▾ shows a faint line in the button's icon color between the two halves, also on the light Create PR button where it was missing, and the git icons in it are a bit larger with a stronger line.
• Team sessions: Search and the team list show only sessions from projects added on this Mac, not every repository Entire lets you read
